$comment: The releases this project measures itself against, and the facts that identify them.
Read by the `Reference releases are intact` step in release-dmg.yml, which fails the
build if any of these tags disappears or moves to a different commit.
GitHub-side tag protection became available when this repository was made public on
2026-08-17 — rulesets need Pro or a public repository, and it is now the latter. This
check is kept alongside rather than replaced by one: a ruleset can stop a tag being
deleted, but it does not record which commit the tag is supposed to point at, nor the
digest of the artifact that was published from it. Those are the facts a fallback point
is actually made of, and they live here.
Three references. v1.0.5 is the floor, v1.0.9 closes the 1.x line, and v2.5.1 is the
current release, made a reference on 2026-09-01 by the owner's decision. A release
cannot record itself — the commit it names is the commit that carries it, and no file
can contain its own hash — so each entry here is added by the commit after the release
it describes.
They used to be spread across the project rather than clustered at its end, and v2.1.0
was the third. It was withdrawn with v2.2.0, v2.3.0 and v2.4.0 on 2026-08-30, and v2.5.0
followed on 2026-09-01 when v2.5.1 replaced it — so the 2.x line is still represented by
its head alone. What that costs is named rather than hidden: a fault introduced this week
is no longer bracketed from below by anything nearer than v1.0.9. The list is kept at
three deliberately; the next reference worth adding is the first 2.x state after this one
that is worth falling back to, and adding it is a decision rather than a consequence of
publishing.
Adding or changing any value below is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff as one.

references.why: First release of the numbering that survives; everything before it was withdrawn.
The second reference: credits the corpus authors, bounds a download that had nothing but the disk to stop it, and is the recent state to fall back to rather than the floor.

The current release and the third reference: `-h` and `-V` answer instead of starting a 71 MiB corpus build, an archive that names one entry twice is refused by name rather than surfacing as a bare AlreadyExists on a path, and a cancellation is heard by the header scan — a quarter of the run that could not be stopped before. The window that reads the package became a real screen with it. It replaced v2.5.0, withdrawn on 2026-09-01: that release was the reference this one is cut from, and a reference cannot be re-cut, so the work took a number of its own and the old reference was retired rather than left standing beside it.
